representation: A fixed five-node graph A-B, A-C, B-D, C-D, D-E whose node sizes encode unvisited, frontier, current and visited states, with a status line naming the queue or stack at each step.
motion: The frontier nodes enlarge, the current node enlarges further, and visited nodes settle at a middle size as BFS runs first and DFS runs second from the same start.
controls: state timeline with pause/continue checkpoints; no numeric slider
checkpoints: DFS uses a stack and reaches E before C
visited set prevents repeats and the orders differ
misconceptionTest: DFS reaches E along A-B-D-E before visiting C, so its order is not shortest-path order; the BFS phase shows D=2 and E=3. At C, neighbor D is skipped because it is already visited, so nodes are not revisited forever.
accessibility: Alt text; keyboard play/pause and checkpoints; every node has a letter label, and the status line names the queue or stack, frontier and visited set in words.
